name: Langtang village co-seismic avalanche (Gorkha earthquake), Nepal
notes: Co-seismic reference: an avalanche triggered by the 2015 Gorkha earthquake, not a spontaneous detachment. The USGS figures come from the 'Regional Background' paragraph of the 2026 Nepal event page, which is preliminary. dammed_river / secondary_surge are non-nullable booleans in the contract; where the retrieved sources do not state them they are recorded as false, meaning 'not established in the retrieved text', not 'established absent'.

source_location.basis: OpenStreetMap Nominatim result for 'Langtang, Rasuwa' (node 976471702), the village destroyed by the avalanche; the source area on Langtang Lirung above 5000 m a.s.l. (USGS) was not located more precisely in the retrieved text

estimates.qualifier: Lacroix (2016) as cited by Fujita et al. (2017): 'a total avalanche volume of 14.38 × 10^6 m3'

source_volume_m3.notes: Fujita et al. (2017) quote Lacroix (2016) for the total avalanche volume; their own DEM work measures the deposits (see bulked_volume_m3). USGS: 'several million cubic meters'. No best because the figure is second-hand in the retrieved text

sources.excerpt: Coseismic avalanches and rockfalls, as well as their simultaneous air blast and muddy flow, killed more than 350 people and destroyed the village of Langtang (Kargel et al., 2016).
sources.title: Anomalous winter-snow-amplified earthquake-induced disaster of the 2015 Langtang avalanche in Nepal

sources.excerpt: This mountain was previously the source of another large debris avalanche in 2015 caused by a M7.8 earthquake. There, several million cubic meters of ice and debris collapsed, starting at 5,000-meter elevation, and fell nearly 1,900 meters, burying a village, and killing more than 200.
